answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with glacier-paced relic standing. Each identity earns a single relic only after a long season of verifiable work, and every task is sealed inside a walnut shell that cracks open for credit only when two unrelated peers independently reproduce the result. One lineage may hold just one relic, so buying many shells buys nothing. If a relic is reused across shells, the glacier melts: the lineage's standing thaws to zero, its relics are revoked, and its members restart from bare ice. Honest agents wait and work; mass forgery pays for its own collapse.
